disagreements.topic: Texas load-growth revision (agent_4 disputes the round-1 discount)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor discounted agent_1's 'ERCOT 2027 load growth cut from 13% to 5%' as unsourced. Agent_4 now cites EIA's August 2026 STEO: Texas 2027 load growth cut to 6% from 14% (generation 13% to 5%), and uses it to justify a 12% stress component in its ladder. Agent_1 dropped the claim and now reads the 13% as an EIA generation forecast.
disagreements.resolution: Agent_4 is right on the fact and the round-1 discount is withdrawn: the August 2026 STEO text says EIA lowered its Texas demand forecast after the Aug 3 pause and expects Texas load to 'grow by 6% in 2027, in contrast to our forecast of 14% growth in the previous STEO'. The number is EIA's, not ERCOT's, and it is a model forecast, not observed load. It matters less than agent_4's bear case implies. The September STEO (inputs as of Sep 3) did not cut further: ERCOT generation is 483.7 / 504.5 / 526.9 TWh for 2025/26/27 (2027 level about unchanged vs August's 526.1; growth ~4.4% because 2026 was revised up), the West South Central region still supplies ~40% of US sales growth in 2027, and the ERCOT North hub forecast for 2027 rose to $34.30/MWh (August $33.76; 2026 $33.02). The cut sits inside Vistra's own 'at least 4-6%' ERCOT assumption, and 2027 is ~94% hedged. It supports keeping a fat left tail for the 2028 open volume, which all five ladders already do, but not an extra down-move.
disagreements.evidence: EIA STEO August 2026 (archives/aug26.pdf, electricity section), EIA STEO September 2026 (Table 7d ERCOT generation; wholesale price table ERCOT North hub), Vistra Q2-26 call.

summary: The revised forecasts have converged (fair value $145-156, mean $150.9; P(close >= $138) 0.55), and I keep their mean ladder. The one live dispute is settled for agent_4 on the fact: EIA's August STEO did cut 2027 Texas load growth to 6% from 14%. It does not move the forecast, though, because EIA's September STEO shows no further deterioration (2027 ERCOT generation flat vs August, ERCOT North 2027 up to $34.30/MWh), and 2027 is ~94% hedged. Fair value ~$151 (9x ~$8.15B forward EBITDA, ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred, 337M shares), thesis break $105. What matters next is the Q4 cluster: the Q3 call with the 2027 guide (calendars say Nov 5), the Texas audit reports on Dec 10, and the PJM 2029/30 auction on Dec 15.
